questions.stem: The Chief Economic Adviser has called for aligning loan-overdue classification norms for MSMEs with their cash-flow cycles. With reference to the Reserve Bank of India's asset classification norms, consider the following statements: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: An account is classified as a Special Mention Account-0 (SMA-0) if payment is overdue for up to 30 days.
SMA-2 classification covers accounts that are overdue between 61 and 90 days.
An account automatically becomes a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) as soon as it is classified as SMA-2, even before completing 90 days overdue.
Banks are required to report the SMA status of borrowers with specified aggregate exposure to the Central Repository of Information on Large Credits (CRILC).
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are accurate per RBI's prudential framework: SMA-0 (up to 30 days), SMA-1 (31-60), SMA-2 (61-90 days overdue), and mandatory SMA reporting to CRILC. Statement 3 is wrong because NPA classification requires an account to remain overdue for more than 90 days, not automatic conversion at SMA-2 entry.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: CEA bats for a review of loan overdue rules for MSMEs
questions.pyqLink: Tests RBI's SMA/NPA asset classification framework, a recurring Economy static concept; similar to UPSC's recurring questions on banking prudential norms.

questions.stem: The RBI raised the repo rate by 25 basis points this week, its first hike since February 2023. With reference to the repo rate as a monetary policy instrument, which one of the following best describes it?
options: The rate at which RBI buys government securities outright from banks to permanently inject liquidity into the banking system.
The rate at which commercial banks lend short-term funds to one another in the interbank call money market.
The minimum rate below which banks are not permitted to lend to their most creditworthy borrowers.
The rate at which RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities as collateral under a repurchase agreement, used to signal monetary policy stance.
questions.explanation: The repo rate is the rate at which RBI provides short-term liquidity to banks against government securities under a repurchase agreement, and changes in it are the primary tool for signalling and transmitting monetary policy stance. Option A describes an outright open market operation, B describes the call money rate, and C describes a lending rate floor like the MCLR, all of which are distinct instruments.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: The week in charts: rate hikes, SIP flows, Airtel’s tariffs
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static definition of repo rate under monetary policy tools, similar to past UPSC questions on RBI's policy instruments (CRR, SLR, repo, reverse repo).

questions.stem: A Kerala High Court order directing an FIR against a former Chief Minister has been criticised by legal experts for overlooking a statutory safeguard. Consider the following two statements:
statements: Statement-I: Prior approval of a competent authority is mandatory before a police officer can conduct an inquiry or investigation into an offence alleged to have been committed by a public servant in discharge of official functions.

Statement-II: This requirement, inserted as Section 17A through the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018, was intended to protect honest public servants from undue harassment while exercising bona fide discretion in official duties.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, inserted by the 2018 amendment, mandates prior approval before police inquiry/investigation into a public servant's official decisions, precisely to shield honest officials from harassment for bona fide discretionary decisions, so Statement-II correctly explains the rationale for Statement-I.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Kerala HC order against former CM Pinarayi Vijayan and others raises a larger question of natural justice, say legal experts
questions.pyqLink: Tests Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, a frequently tested statutory-safeguard provision in Polity prelims.

questions.stem: A Padma Shri awardee's enumeration form was rejected under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls for not linking her entry to her parents' 2002 records. With reference to electoral rolls and voter registration, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls is conducted by the Election Commission of India under powers derived from the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
A person not registered as a voter in 2002 can never be enrolled in the electoral roll at any later date, irrespective of citizenship status.
Under Article 326 of the Constitution, every citizen not less than 18 years of age and not otherwise disqualified is entitled to be registered as a voter.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — electoral roll preparation and revision is carried out by the ECI under the Representation of the People Act, 1950. Statement 3 is correct — Article 326 guarantees universal adult suffrage to all eligible citizens. Statement 2 is false, since the article itself shows people who were adults in 2002 but unregistered then being enrolled as voters years later.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: SIR: Padma Shri awardee Sunitha Krishnan’s enumeration form rejected
questions.pyqLink: Tests the constitutional basis of universal adult suffrage (Article 326) and the statutory basis of electoral roll revision, a recurring Polity static theme.

questions.stem: The EU and China have reached an understanding to moderate hybrid car exports after the EU considered 'safeguard measures' against a surge in Chinese imports. With reference to trade remedy measures under WTO rules, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Anti-dumping duties can be imposed only on goods exported by countries that are members of a customs union with the importing country.

Safeguard measures can be imposed on imports from all trading partners when a sudden surge in imports causes or threatens serious injury to the domestic industry, without needing to prove unfair trade practice.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct: under the WTO Agreement on Safeguards, a member can restrict imports from all sources if a sudden surge causes or threatens serious injury, even if the trade is otherwise fair. Statement 1 is false — anti-dumping duties apply to exporters found selling below normal value in any country, with no requirement of a customs union relationship.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: EU-China trade breakthrough: Beijing agrees to moderate hybrid car exports by more than half | Here's what we know
questions.pyqLink: Tests the distinction between WTO safeguard measures and anti-dumping duties, a recurring International Relations/Economy static trade-law concept.

questions.stem: India exercised its Right of Reply at the UN's First Committee on nuclear weapons and disarmament. Consider the following pairs of disarmament-related institutions and their descriptions: How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: The sole multilateral forum of the international community for negotiating disarmament treaties, based in Geneva
First Committee of the UN General Assembly
Deals with Disarmament and International Security issues
A treaty-based body established under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty to regulate global nuclear trade
A specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for verifying compliance with the treaty
questions.explanation: Pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched. Pair 3 is wrong because the Nuclear Suppliers Group is a voluntary export-control regime formed in 1974-75 outside the NPT framework, not a treaty body under it. Pair 4 is wrong because the CTBTO Preparatory Commission is an independent international organisation, not a UN specialized agency, and the treaty itself has not entered into force.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Nuclear weapons must not be treated as 'routine instruments of statecraft': India slams Pak at UN
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional architecture of global nuclear non-proliferation and disarmament bodies, similar to past UPSC questions distinguishing NSG, NPT, CTBT and the Wassenaar Arrangement.

questions.stem: A Panama-flagged oil tanker was attacked at Sharjah Anchorage in the Gulf region. With reference to the geography of this maritime region, consider the following statements: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and is one of the world's most significant oil transit chokepoints.
Sharjah is among the emirates of the United Arab Emirates that has no coastline on the Persian Gulf.
The Strait of Malacca is a chokepoint located between the Arabian Peninsula and the Iranian mainland.
Qatar is a landlocked country without direct access to the Persian Gulf.
questions.explanation: Only statement 1 is correct. Sharjah has a Persian Gulf coastline (besides Khor Fakkan on the Gulf of Oman), so statement 2 is false; the Strait of Malacca lies between the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra and Singapore, not the Persian Gulf, so statement 3 is false; and Qatar is a peninsula with a Persian Gulf coastline, not landlocked, so statement 4 is false.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: All Indian crew members safe after oil tanker attacked at Sharjah Anchorage: Sarbananda Sonowal
questions.pyqLink: Tests the geography of Persian Gulf chokepoints and littoral states, a recurring Geography static theme linked to global energy-security news.

questions.stem: With reference to the fundamental right to peaceful assembly in India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Article 19(1)(b) of the Constitution guarantees to all citizens the right to assemble peaceably and without arms.
Reasonable restrictions on the right to assembly under Article 19(3) can be imposed only directly by Parliament through a law, and never through an order of an executive authority.
Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which earlier empowered magistrates to restrict public assembly, has now been replaced by Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — Article 19(1)(b) is the textual source of the right. Statement 3 is correct, as confirmed by the article: Section 144 CrPC has been replaced by Section 163 BNSS. Statement 2 is incorrect because Article 19(3) restrictions are validly imposed through executive orders issued under a parent statute (like Section 144 CrPC/Section 163 BNSS itself), not only by direct parliamentary enactment — this is exactly the mechanism the Supreme Court examined in Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan v. Union of India (2018).
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: CJP protest: The right to protest, and what happens when police deny permission
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 19(1)(b)/19(3) and the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan precedent on public order restrictions, similar to UPSC's recurring questions on fundamental rights and reasonable restrictions.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) reservation:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections was introduced through the 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019.
EWS reservation is applicable only to persons not already covered under the existing reservation schemes for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes.
The income and asset ceilings for determining EWS eligibility are explicitly specified in the Constitution itself.
The Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of the EWS reservation in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022).
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct and well-established static facts. Statement 3 is incorrect — the Constitution (103rd Amendment) only enables EWS reservation; the specific income/asset criteria are prescribed through government notifications/rules (as seen in J&K's 2019 amendment to its Reservation Rules), not the Constitution.
questions.subject: Social Issues & Schemes
questions.sourceTitle: Regional imbalance, different yardsticks: Controversy over J&K’s EWS certificates
questions.pyqLink: Tests the 103rd Constitutional Amendment and Janhit Abhiyan judgment on EWS reservation, a recurring Polity/Social Justice theme.

questions.stem: With reference to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A of the Constitution of India.
All decisions of the GST Council must be taken by consensus, as the Constitution does not provide for any voting mechanism within the Council.
None
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — Article 279A, inserted by the 101st Amendment, constitutes the GST Council. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 279A(9) prescribes a weighted voting mechanism (Centre 1/3rd weightage, states 2/3rd, decisions needing three-fourths majority of weighted votes) for occasions when consensus is not reached.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Delivery completed: On the GST Council meet, reforms
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 279A and the GST Council's voting structure, a frequently tested cooperative-federalism institution.

questions.stem: The European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) has recently come under a US investigation. Which one of the following best describes the underlying mechanism of CBAM?
options: It requires EU importers to declare the embedded emissions of covered imported goods and pay a carbon price equivalent to what domestic EU producers pay under the EU Emissions Trading System.
It is a voluntary carbon-offset scheme under which exporting countries can buy carbon credits to reduce the tariff applicable to their goods.
It is a direct subsidy paid by the EU to its own carbon-intensive manufacturers to offset their compliance costs under the EU Emissions Trading System.
It is a WTO-administered multilateral agreement harmonising carbon pricing across all member countries' traded goods.
questions.explanation: CBAM links the carbon price on imports to the price domestic EU producers pay under the EU Emissions Trading System, based on declared embedded emissions, as described in the article. It is not a voluntary offset scheme, not an EU domestic subsidy, and not a WTO multilateral arrangement — it is a unilateral EU border measure that has itself generated trade friction, including the US investigation.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: US begins probe into EU's carbon border tax: How India could benefit
questions.pyqLink: Tests the concept of carbon border adjustment/carbon pricing linked to an Emissions Trading System, an increasingly tested Economy-Environment interface topic.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the regulation of prescription drug advertising in India:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Schedule H drugs under the Drugs Rules, 1945 can be sold at retail only against the prescription of a registered medical practitioner.
The existing Drugs Rules, 1945 already prohibit manufacturers of Schedule H, H1 and X drugs from advertising them without prior sanction of the Central Government.
The Drugs Technical Advisory Board is a statutory body constituted under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.
The proposed amendment removes the requirement of prior government sanction for advertising Schedule H1 drugs.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct static/legal facts about the Drugs Rules, 1945 and the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. Statement 4 is incorrect and reverses the actual proposal — the draft amendment extends the existing advertising-sanction requirement to retailers, wholesalers and distributors, it does not remove the requirement for anyone.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Centre proposes tighter curbs on advertising of prescription drugs
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Drugs Rules, 1945 schedules (H, H1, X) and the statutory status of DTAB under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

questions.stem: Consider the following two statements in the context of the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize awarded to jurist Navi Pillay:
statements: Statement-I: The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize citation credited Navi Pillay with being instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted.

Statement-II: The International Criminal Court, established under the Rome Statute, has universal jurisdiction to prosecute the nationals of any state in the world, regardless of whether that state has ratified the Statute or the matter has been referred to it.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct, directly reflected in the Nobel Committee's citation. Statement-II is incorrect — the ICC's jurisdiction is not universal; it can ordinarily prosecute only nationals of states that are parties to the Rome Statute, or situations referred to it by the UN Security Council, or where a state otherwise accepts its jurisdiction.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Nobel Peace Prize 2026: How Navi Pillay's work on genocide 'held states and leaders accountable'
questions.pyqLink: Tests the jurisdictional limits of the International Criminal Court under the Rome Statute, a recurring IR/International Law static concept.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of criminal law provisions mentioned in the context of recent legal changes in India:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Section 144, Code of Criminal Procedure (public nuisance/danger orders)
Section 438, Code of Criminal Procedure (anticipatory bail)
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correctly matched — Section 144 CrPC corresponds to Section 163 BNSS (as the article confirms), murder under IPC Section 302 corresponds to BNS Section 103, and anticipatory bail under CrPC Section 438 corresponds to BNSS Section 482. Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: the provision addressing acts endangering the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India (replacing sedition) is Section 152 of the BNS, not Section 111, which instead deals with organised crime.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: CJP protest: The right to protest, and what happens when police deny permission
questions.pyqLink: Tests the correspondence between the repealed IPC/CrPC provisions and the new Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita/Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, a high-priority current-static fusion topic since 2024.

questions.stem: The Madhya Pradesh High Court struck down a law raising OBC reservation from 14% to 27%, citing the Supreme Court's ceiling on reservations. In this context, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Supreme Court in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992) capped total reservations at 50%, permitting exceptions only in extraordinary circumstances.
The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 introduced 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections as an exception operating outside the 50% ceiling.
Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in local body elections is governed exclusively by Article 334 of the Constitution.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Indra Sawhney (1992) fixed the 50% ceiling, breachable only in extraordinary circumstances, the exact ground on which the MP HC rejected the 14%-to-27% hike. Statement 2 is correct: the EWS quota was upheld in Janhit Abhiyan (2022) as a permissible exception to the 50% rule. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 334 governs reservation of seats for SC/ST (and formerly Anglo-Indians) in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, not local bodies, which are covered by Articles 243D and 243T.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Striking down 27% quota, Madhya Pradesh High Court cites OBC chief ministers, quotes Rousseau
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Indra Sawhney 50% ceiling and EWS exception, similar to UPSC 2022 questions on reservation provisions.

questions.stem: A probe into alleged irregularities in Bhopal liquor-shop contracts has drawn attention to how states tax alcohol. With reference to this, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Duties of excise on alcoholic liquors for human consumption fall under the State List of the Seventh Schedule.
The Goods and Services Tax (GST) subsumed excise duty on alcoholic liquor for human consumption, bringing it under the unified GST regime.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Entry 51 of the State List empowers states to levy excise duty on alcoholic liquors for human consumption, which is why Madhya Pradesh's Commercial Tax/Excise Department handles such contracts. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 366(12A) explicitly excludes alcoholic liquor for human consumption from GST; it continues to be taxed separately by states through excise duty and VAT.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Why Madhya Pradesh relieved Deputy Chief Minister’s OSD
questions.pyqLink: Tests Seventh Schedule tax entries and GST exclusions, a recurring area since UPSC 2017 and 2022 questions on GST Council and taxation powers.

questions.stem: An infant orangutan seized from a Dombivli apartment is set to be repatriated to Indonesia after rehabilitation in India. Consider the following pairs:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Listed in Appendix I of CITES, prohibiting commercial trade in wild-caught specimens
Schedule I species accorded the highest degree of legal protection in India
Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre (Vantara)
Managed exclusively by the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, with no role for the state government
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched: orangutans are CITES Appendix I species, India's Wildlife (Protection) Act gives Schedule I species the strictest protection, and the GZRRC is indeed located in Jamnagar. Pair 4 is wrong: the Balasaheb Thackeray Gorewada International Zoological Park at Nagpur is run jointly with the Maharashtra state zoo authority, not exclusively by the Union ministry.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: From Maharashtra apartment to Indonesian wilds: Rescued orangutan set to return home
questions.pyqLink: Tests CITES appendices and Wildlife Protection Act schedules, similar to UPSC's recurring species-protection-status questions (e.g., 2023 questions on wildlife schedules).

questions.stem: A Punjab-manufactured Vande Bharat trainset completed a 180 kmph trial under the supervision of the Chief Commissioner of Railway Safety (CRS). Which one of the following best describes the institutional position of the Commission of Railway Safety?
options: It is a wing of the Railway Board that certifies rolling stock before commercial induction.
It functions under the Ministry of Civil Aviation and certifies safety standards for all modes of transport, including roadways.
It functions under the Ministry of Civil Aviation for administrative purposes, even though its mandate is railway safety, so as to keep it independent of the Railway Board it inspects.
It is a statutory tribunal under the Railways Act, 1989 that adjudicates compensation claims arising from railway accidents.
questions.explanation: The Commission of Railway Safety is kept under the administrative control of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, not the Ministry of Railways, precisely to preserve its independence as the inspecting and safety-certifying authority over the railway system it oversees. It does not certify other transport modes (ruling out option B), is not part of the Railway Board (ruling out A), and is not a compensation tribunal (that role belongs to Railway Claims Tribunal, ruling out D).
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Vande Bharat train manufactured in Punjab completes 180 kmph trial on Mathura-Nagda section
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional placement of CRS, a recurring static-fact trap similar to questions on regulatory bodies placed outside their natural ministry.

questions.stem: The Shillong Literary Festival will showcase Meghalaya's Khasi, Jaintia and Garo literary traditions. With reference to the tribes of Meghalaya, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Khasi and Jaintia communities traditionally follow a matrilineal system of inheritance.
The Garo language belongs to the Tibeto-Burman family, while Khasi belongs to the Austroasiatic (Mon-Khmer) family.
Meghalaya has three Autonomous District Councils under the Sixth Schedule, covering the Khasi Hills, Jaintia Hills and Garo Hills.
The traditional Khasi living root bridges are found mainly in the West Jaintia Hills district.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Khasi-Jaintia society is matrilineal, Garo is Tibeto-Burman while Khasi is Austroasiatic, and Meghalaya has three Sixth Schedule Autonomous District Councils. Statement 4 is wrong: living root bridges are concentrated in the East Khasi Hills district (around Cherrapunji, Mawlynnong and Nongriat), not West Jaintia Hills.

questions.stem: Sonam Wangchuk highlighted his continued work on artificial glaciers for water security in Ladakh. With reference to Ladakh's physical geography, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Artificial glaciers (ice stupas) store winter stream water as conical ice towers that melt gradually to supply irrigation water in spring and summer.
Ladakh receives the bulk of its scant annual precipitation from the southwest monsoon between June and September.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the ice-stupa technique pioneered in Ladakh freezes diverted stream water in winter for use during the sowing season. Statement 2 is wrong: Ladakh lies in the Himalayan rain shadow, cut off from the southwest monsoon; its scant precipitation comes mainly as winter snowfall from western disturbances, which is why it is classified as a cold desert.
